text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sudden 3x token latency surge in runtime-prod around 14:05-14:20 UTC, throughput dropped ~40%. Dashboards look partially empty for that window, traces are very sparse. Anyone oncall?

mira: I can take a look. initial observation: traces are sampled down in the collector, looks like sampling config flipped to 1% for that time range. Investigating if that was manual or auto.

tj: Profiling the runtime for the same window — profiler shows kernel-selector fallback from fast-simd to reference kernel for model=redwood-stable-7b. The fallback correlates with very small batch sizes (1-3 tokens) and repeated KV cache evictions.

sasha: On the infra side, tenant t-44 had a burst of long-prefix requests starting 14:04, GPU 0/1 pinned at ~99% for ~8 minutes. Could be noisy tenant causing KV thrash and forcing the kernel choice.

alex: dashboard mismatch: per-route token counters show normal ingress, but GPU throughput (tokens/s) drops. That suggests work is queued or being serialized on device.

mira: Confirmed: collector sampling had been set to 0.01 earlier (ops change) and a CICD job pushed a new sampling conf at 14:00 that mistakenly applied to prod. That's why traces are sparse and we can't see span-level routing handoffs.

tj: From the profiler stack: hot path shows spin on kv_cache::evict_loop and then kernel_selector::choose -> picks reference path because quantized-tile kernel mispredicted due to tiny seq_len distribution. I can attach a short extract: ```
[14:06:12] kv_cache::miss_rate=0.42
[14:06:12] kernel_selector: chosen=kernel_ref, latency=12.4ms
[14:06:12] kernel_selector: alt=kernel_simd, estimated=4.1ms but incompatible with batch shape
```

sasha: ops mitigation idea: throttling the offender tenant to cap active concurrent streams at 20 and enable route-based fallback to smaller model variant. I can apply a temporary policy.

alex: Let's do these steps now: 1) Mira full sampling for 15m so we can get traces. 2) Sasha throttle tenant t-44. 3) TJ capture a 2-minute profiler window with KV debug on. 4) Open an incident ticket and link traces.

mira: Running full sampling now (15m): ```kubectl -n observability set env deployment/collector TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0 --record``` will flip to 100%. Doing it.

sasha: Applying throttle: ```routes apply --tenant t-44 --max-concurrency 20 --reason "incident 1769001112"``` done, policy propagated to edge within 45s.

tj: Starting profiler capture with kv debug: ```profiler capture --duration 120 --tags kernel,kv,selector --out /tmp/prof-1769001112.pprof``` started.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INF-2142 — latency surge + observability gaps. Priority P2. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2142

alex: Initial results after mitigations: GPU utilization dropped to ~70% on affected hosts, latency back down to baseline after ~90s, throughput recovered. Traces coming in now with full spans. Good. :thumbsup:

mira: Postmortem notes to add: (a) risk of applying global sampling changes via CICD job, (b) lack of per-tenant kv eviction metrics in main dashboard, (c) kernel-selector should log fallback reasons at INFO so we correlate faster.

tj: Follow-ups I’ll own: add a histogram of batch size distribution to runtime dashboard, increase KV eviction and miss-rate retention to 7d, and add an alert: kv_miss_rate > 0.15 && kernel_fallback_count > 5 => page SRE.

sasha: Ops follow-ups: build a temporary automatic throttling rule when a tenant causes sustained GPU>92% for >3min, and add a routing policy to divert to dedicated pool for heavy prefixes.

alex: I'll draft the incident summary and link profiler + traces. We'll schedule a 30m runbook review with eng-runtime and observability tomorrow. Thanks everyone.

mira: quick note — add to runbook: before lowering sampling make sure `ci/observability/overrides` is gated by a prod-ops review. Learned that the hard way.

alex: filed runbook change in INF-2142, pinging eng-runtime to join postmortem meeting.

sasha: :rocket:
